espn.short: Dicker went 3-for-3 on field-goal attempts and made his only PAT during Sunday's 44-22 loss to Houston.
espn.long: Dicker was able to make multiple field-goal tries for the third straight game and fifth time this season. The kicker did all his damage in the first half, converting field goals from 52, 33 and 43 yards before the break. Dicker has now gone 15-for-17 on field-goal attempts, including 1-for-2 from 50-plus yards, over eight contests so far during the 2026 campaign.

sections.Intro: Cameron Lawrence Dicker (born May 6, 2000), nicknamed "Dicker the Kicker," is an American professional football placekicker for the Los Angeles Chargers of the National Football League (NFL). He was an All-Big 12 kicker and punter for the Texas Longhorns, where he holds the school record for field goals made, in college football. Dicker was signed by the Los Angeles Rams as an undrafted free agent in 2022. He has also been a member of the Baltimore Ravens and Philadelphia Eagles. Dicker is the most accurate kicker in NFL history by field goal percentage (92.8%), and is the only NFL player born in Hong Kong.
sections.Early life:
Cameron Lawrence Dicker was born on May 6, 2000, in Hong Kong, to Kelly and Rachel Dicker. He has a sister named Annabelle. His parents were from Seattle but were working in China. Dicker spent the first 11 years of his life in Shanghai, where his father worked. Dicker grew up watching soccer and is a fan of Liverpool F.C. In 2011, when he was 11, his family moved to Austin, Texas.
Dicker did not play football until the fifth grade as part of an ex-pat youth league in Shanghai. He moved to Austin and played on the middle school team, as a left guard. 
During his high school career at Austin's Lake Travis High School, Dicker was a two-time all-state selection and was the starting kicker for three seasons and the starting punter for two seasons, winning the Texas 6A Division I State Championship in 2016 with teammates Garrett Wilson and Charlie Brewer and was state runner-up in 2015. Dicker had 331 points, going 34-of-43 on field goal attempts and 229-of-232 on extra point attempts. He also set a Lake Travis High School record with a 53-yard field goal. Dicker was ranked the number four kicker in the nation by 247Sports and the number 16 kicker nationally by ESPN in the 2018 class. On May 4, 2017, Dicker committed to Texas.
Dicker also played soccer at Lake Travis, helping them to the 2015 State Championship game.
sections.College career:
Dicker played college football at the University of Texas where he earned immediate playing time, winning the starting role as a freshman. Dicker kicked his first career game-winning field goal against #7 Oklahoma. In that game, he gained notoriety as "Dicker the Kicker" (by play-by-play announcer Gus Johnson of Fox Sports) when he kicked the game-winning 40-yard field goal in the Red River Showdown. For that kick, Dicker was named the Big 12 Special Teams player of the week for the first time. He was named Big 12 Special Teams player of the week against after the Texas Tech game when he was perfect for kicking, hitting field goals of 46 and 52 yards. The 52 yard field goal Dicker hit was tied for the third longest by a freshman in school history. He went 18-of-25 on field goals and 51-of-52 on extra points that year, earning 2018 second-team All-Big 12 honors, honorable mention as Big 12 Special Teams Player of the Year and All-Rookie Academic All-Big 12 honors. Dicker's field goals kicked and attempted both led the Big 12 that year, and it was the most field goals kicked by a freshman in Texas history. His 97 points scored was the 2nd most by a freshman in school history. That season, Dicker helped the Longhorns make it to the 2018 Big 12 Championship game, to upset Georgia in the 2019 Sugar Bowl and finish ranked #9.
Before the 2019 season started, Dicker was placed on the Lou Groza Award watchlist. That season, he kicked a college career long 57 yard field goal against Rice, the sixth longest in Big 12 history and seventh longest in school history at the time. The only Longhorn to kick a longer field goal is Russell Erxleben. A few weeks later against Kansas, Dicker made all six of his extra point attempts and both of his field goal attempts, including kicking a walk-off 33-yard game winner and earned Big 12 Special Teams player of the week honors. He helped the Longhorns to a win in the 2019 Alamo Bowl and a #25 finish in the rankings. Dicker was also an Honorable Mention as a kicker on the All-Big 12 team, led the conference in extra point attempts and makes and earned First Team Academic All-Big 12 honors. He was perfect for extra points on the season, tying the school's extra point percentage record for a season. 
Dicker earned second-team All-Big 12 honors in 2020 as he again led the conference in extra point attempts and makes. When Ryan Bujcevski suffered a torn ACL against West Virginia, Dicker also took over punting duties. He again helped the Longhorns to a bowl win, in the 2020 Alamo Bowl, and a top 25 ranking (#19/#20) in the polls. During the Alamo Bowl, Dicker set the record for the longest field goal in Alamo Bowl history, kicking a 53-yarder that was also the second longest field goal in a bowl game in school history. For the third year in a row, he was the team's scoring leader, and he again earned First Team Academic All-Big 12 honors. 
In 2021, Dicker continued to punt as Bujcevski recovered from his injury. Before the season started, he was again placed on the Lou Groza Award watchlist. Against Texas Tech, Dicker kicked 10 extra points, tied for the fifth most in a game in Big 12 history and tied for first in school history for both extra points attempted and made in a game. He was named the Big 12 co-Special Teams player of the week after the Kansas game when he made all eight of his extra points and had two punts for 90 yards. In the next game, Dicker had four field goals against TCU, which tied for fifth for the most field goals in a single game in school history. The following week, he had a career-long 78 yard punt, the fifth longest in school history. Against Oklahoma State a week later, Dicker averaged 51.7 ypp, the seventh best single-game punting average in school history, on seven punts including the school's sixth longest punt ever of 77 yards. In November, he was named a Ray Guy Award semifinalist for his punting as he led the nation in et punting average. At the end of the season, Dicker was named 1st Team All-Big 12 as a punter after averaging 46.8 ypp (third best season in school history behind Michael Dickson in 2016 and 2017), was honorable mention as Big 12 Special Teams Player of the Year, honorable mention as a kicker, made the First Team Academic All-Big 12 team for the fourth consecutive year and was a Campbell Trophy Award semifinalist. Across the 2020 season, he made 70 extra point attempts in a row and 12 field goals in a row - both were the fourth longest such streaks in school history at the time. Dicker also connected on a career high 86.7% of field goal attempts - the fourth best for a season in school history.
Dicker finished his career as the highest scoring kicker in school history and third on the all-time scoring list with 386 points, behind Cedric Benson and Ricky Williams. In the final game of his career, Dicker broke Phil Dawson's school record for the most field goals made (60) in a career and tied him for most field goal attempts (79). He also finished second in extra point attempts (210), second for extra points made (206) and fourth in field goal accuracy (75.9%). Dicker's four career field goals of longer than 50 yards tied him for 6th in school history.
On January 19, 2022, Dicker declared for the 2022 NFL draft. On February 5, he participated in the 2022 Senior Bowl.
sections.Personal life: Dicker is a Christian. He is engaged to Annie Buerk. Dicker was given the nickname "Dicker the Kicker" by his seventh grade science teacher.
